content.text:
1	---
2	name: kimi-cli-kaola-project-runner
3	description: Use when the controlling Agent should communicate with a Kimi Code CLI main conversation through an exact owned ACP session by starting it, reading evidence, sending Agent-selected prompts or keys, reading replies, and stopping only that session.
4	---
5	
6	# Kimi CLI Kaola Project Runner
7	
8	This Skill is a communication driver for Kimi CLI. It gives the controlling Agent a
9	measured ACP channel to one exact owned session; it does not choose commands, Workflow modes, cadence, state, approvals,
10	retries, or completion policy. The separate Skill `kaola-project-runner` (display name Project
11	Runner) is the main orchestrator when a host Agent is supervising workers; this Skill stays
12	transport-only.
13	
14	## Transport
15	
16	ACP is the only transport (Issue #130). The ACP command is `kimi acp`; prompts travel over its stdio JSON-RPC, never shell eval. Login is a human act outside the Runner and needs no terminal. This platform's ACP quirks are in [references/acp.md](references/acp.md) — open it when a quirk matters. A request for the retired PTY transport is refused with `transport-pty-retired` and changes nothing.
17	
18	| `mutation_status` | Safe interpretation |
19	|---|---|
20	| `not_started` | No prompt write began. |
21	| `accepted` | The agent accepted the prompt. |
22	| `in_progress` | Work may already be mutating state. |
23	| `completed` | The turn reached a reported stop reason. |
24	| `unknown` | Partial mutation cannot be ruled out. |
25	
26	Runner never auto-falls back or resends, and never restarts or resumes a session on its own. Read the receipt and decide whether another prompt is appropriate.
27	
28	## Communication loop
29	
30	Resolve this Skill's installed directory once and call its scripts by absolute path — the install
31	destination may contain spaces, and the user's project is passed only through `--repo` (relative
32	paths in these references resolve against the Skill, never the project cwd). Progressive
33	disclosure: open a reference only when the current operation needs it, run the scripts and never read their source, and prefer bounded
34	receipts (`observe`, `status`, `capture --lines`) over whole-history dumps — `capture --full` is an
35	explicit, unbounded request:
36	
37	```bash
38	SKILL_DIR="/absolute/path/to/kimi-cli-kaola-project-runner"   # the directory containing this file
39	REPO="/abs/canonical/root"   # canonical Git root, not a linked worktree
40	SESSION="<exact-name>"   # under Project Runner: <platform>-<CODE>-i<ISSUE>-<purpose>
41	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" preflight --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
42	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" start --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
43	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" observe --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
44	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" capture --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION" --lines 200
45	```
46	
47	The controlling Agent owns model selection for each `start`. This Skill declares its per-run
48	presets — `--tier default` (**Kimi K3**: `kimi-code/k3`, thinking=max) and `--tier kimi-k2-8` (**Kimi K2.8**: `kimi-code/kimi-for-coding`, thinking=max) — and `default` applies whenever nothing more specific was chosen. Pass
49	another `--tier` when the human or an existing authorization — the default-authorized Worker pool included —
50	names that preset; never infer one from code size, failures, elapsed time, or your own assessment.
51	An undeclared name is refused (`tier-not-declared`), never resolved to `default`.
52	
53	An explicit user model choice always wins: pass it with `--model ID`, adding `--effort LEVEL` only
54	when the user also named an effort. A bare explicit `--model` leaves the runtime's native effort
55	alone — never attach a preset's effort to a different model. If the user picks a model ID that
56	already encodes effort or Fast (such as a `-fast` variant), pass it as-is; the Runner does not
57	invent extra effort or Fast configuration for it.
58	
59	Fast is OFF by default. Pass `--fast on` only on an explicit user request for Fast; this platform's
60	Fast support: no native Fast toggle; speed-named catalog models such as kimi-code/kimi-for-coding-highspeed are explicit model choices, not a Fast switch. Fast and tier are independent selections. When a native fast model
61	ID is what the user explicitly selected, it counts as the explicit Fast selection — report the
62	conflict honestly if it is also passed with `--fast off`.
63	
64	`preflight` and `start` report the requested and resolved selection, and `start` what it applied
65	(`config_application`, `effective_selection`), including unavailable, unsupported, and unknown
66	outcomes; `observe`/`status` show the agent's `configOptions` `currentValue`. `--resume`/`--continue`
67	preserve the saved native session model and effort unless the caller supplies `--tier`, `--model`,
68	or `--effort`; Fast stays a per-run request (off unless explicitly on). All of this is per-run
69	input and never rewrites global CLI configuration. A mismatch or unreadable actual model remains
70	evidence for the Agent and does not disable the communication channel.
71	
72	`preflight` reports runtime and optional Kaola carrier evidence. Missing Workflow commands,
73	configuration health, account state, activity hints, or a changed
74	snapshot do not authorize or block starting the CLI communication channel.
75	
76	Use the evidence internally to choose the next communication action. Do not narrate raw holder,
77	process, snapshot, model, or activity fields in user progress updates; report only visible
78	task progress, an actual transport failure, or a decision that genuinely needs the user.
79	
80	After reading current evidence, the controlling Agent chooses what to send:
81	
82	```bash
83	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" send --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION" --text '<agent-selected prompt>'
84	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" observe --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
85	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" capture --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION" --lines 200
86	```
87	
88	## Steering a running turn
89	
90	Kimi CLI's ACP surface exposes no native mid-turn entry, so a bare `steer`
91	refuses and writes nothing. The available path is the composite, which you
92	choose explicitly:
93	
94	```bash
95	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" steer --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION" \
96	  --steer-mode interrupt --text '<redirection>'
97	```
98	
99	It **cancels** the running turn, confirms it stopped, then sends your text as the
100	next turn on the same session, which keeps the conversation's context. That is
101	interrupted-then-continued, never injection: work in progress stops and may have
102	left partial side effects (`side_effects_possible`). An unconfirmed cancel sends
103	nothing and reports `unknown`. See [references/steering.md](references/steering.md).
104	
105	## Cancel and permissions
106	
107	`key --key escape` (or `cancel`) cancels the running turn; there are no other native keys, menus,
108	or editor replacement. Settle a pending permission `request_id` with
109	`permit [--request-id ID] --option OPTION_ID` (an option the request offers); omitting `--option`
110	answers `cancelled`, which denies. Read the resulting output before choosing another action.
111	
112	Permission default: `start` sets ACP `mode=yolo`; `--permission-mode MODE` sets another advertised `mode` value.
113	
114	When the Agent decides the exact session is finished, end only that owned session:
115	
116	```bash
117	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" stop --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
118	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" status --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
119	```
120	
121	Use `--force` only when the Agent explicitly chooses forced containment for this exact owned
122	session. Never use broad session/process cleanup, and never reconstruct ownership from process
123	names or fuzzy session matches.
124	
125	## Ending, releasing, and resuming
126	
127	The controlling Agent owns every completion judgment; the Runner executes the chosen operation
128	and reports the true result. These are operation facts, never gates:
129	
130	- A finished reply is not a finished task: an `end_turn` event, an idle terminal, or a
131	  successful `send` receipt never establishes completion.
132	- `stop` releases the owned runtime (the ACP holder and its agent). It never deletes CLI
133	  history, session records, work artifacts, or unrelated resources. Judge success by the
134	  `stop`/`status` result evidence, not by a completed call.
135	- Before stopping, the Agent may keep available resume facts (platform, canonical repo, any
136	  reported native session ID, outcome, remaining work) from existing receipts and Workflow
137	  records. The native session ID is the CLI's own conversation identifier, never the Runner's
138	  `--session` name. Missing identifiers never block a chosen `stop`.
139	- Later work resumes by the Agent's choice: `start --resume <native-session-id>`,
140	  `start --continue` for the platform's latest conversation, or a fresh `start` plus existing
141	  records where the platform cannot resume.
142	
143	## Optional Kaola Workflow
144	
145	Ordinary Workflow-backed work binds `--repo` to the consuming project's canonical Git root and asks this CLI to invoke its installed
146	`workflow-next`, so that runtime's Workflow creates or recovers the child worktree; this Skill only
147	transports the exact session. Linked-worktree starts, outer-prepared bundles, and existing-run
148	recovery are Agent decisions, not transport gates. A session already in a child worktree is advisory: preserve work, then continue,
149	stop/restart at root, or use another Workflow recovery path. Installation for another runtime alone
150	does not establish availability here.
151	
152	## Evidence boundary
153	
154	- `capture`, events, process facts, permission facts, activity hints, and snapshot changes are
155	  evidence for the Agent.
156	- Exact session ownership, platform/repository identity, holder identity, prompt fingerprinting,
157	  and outbound redaction are transport integrity checks.
158	- The Runner never classifies evidence into permission to act. The Agent handles every runtime or
159	  Workflow problem after reading the evidence.
160	- No invocation implicitly starts `workflow-next`, installs commands, materializes repository files,
161	  creates a heartbeat, or selects recurring behavior. The Agent may send any of those commands when
162	  it decides they serve the user's task.
163	
164	See [references/platform.md](references/platform.md) for Kimi CLI launch/observation facts
165	and [references/acp.md](references/acp.md) for the structured ACP command surface.

4	---
5	
6	# Project Runner
7	
8	This Skill is the main control-plane Skill. It is not a platform Runner and has
9	no transport adapter. The ten platform Runner Skills are workers: they only
10	identify, start, send, wait, permit, observe, capture, and stop an exact owned
11	session. Kaola-Workflow, when used, owns worker-side claim, mission ledger,
12	child worktree, finalize, archive, and sink.

179	   [qa-evidence.md](references/qa-evidence.md) unless the current version is
180	   already in context. Planned dispatch (research, QA, report or
181	   implementation) uses `execute`
182	   ([dispatch-collect.md](references/dispatch-collect.md)): it starts absent
183	   seats at the preset `--tier` and records their facts. Direct Runner
184	   `start`/`send` is standalone, degraded or same-assignment recovery
185	   (zcode-host-dispatch.md). No permission-mode override unless the human
186	   wrote one. One dispatch prompt per ready session. External knowledge gap behind a route, obstacle, failure or QA question: [public-research.md](references/public-research.md). You still accept and exact-stop. State the task,
187	   working location, write ownership, constraints, delivery requirements, and
188	   the doc-impact call in its prompt, plus whether Workflow is on. That prompt
189	   carries the assignment only: never orchestration policy or the seat roster.
190	   The worker must not self-finalize before acceptance; irreversible or value
191	   choices print `HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED` and wait. Merely seeing a
192	   worktree or ledger is not write authorization. Same-file collaboration needs explicit
193	   coordination and an integrator, not a blanket disjointness rule. Do not
194	   expand the authorized goal or duplicate claims. Pass still-valid candidate
195	   evidence; recheck changed/invalidated facts or actual gaps. Keep required
196	   project/release checks. Substantive failure: [task-failure.md](references/task-failure.md).
197	   One run claims one real issue: never a bundle claim, worktree, ledger or
198	   session spanning several, and collaborating workers share that issue's run under
199	   distinct names. Choose the real open issue before start, name the session
200	   `<platform>-<CODE>-i<ISSUE>-<purpose>` (`droid-KT-i274-parser`) with `CODE` the
201	   heartbeat's declared project short code, verify it in the start receipt, and
202	   keep the rule on later dispatches and restarts. Hosts, diagnostics and
203	   issue-less tasks carry no issue number and never an invented one. Detail:
204	   [issue-dispatch.md](references/issue-dispatch.md).
205	3. **Accept the delivery.** Mission-frontier done triggers review, not automatic finalize. When a worker
206	   claims completion, judge its actual diff, checks, docs and run records
207	   against that assignment under the effective global Workflow rules. Reuse
208	   sufficient evidence for this candidate; return only concrete routine deviations,
209	   omissions or invalidated evidence to that worker, and never finalize on
210	   incomplete evidence or lowered assertions. Worker prose, idle, green CI or
211	   a successful script exit is not acceptance, and acceptance is not project
212	   QA: you pick when aggregate QA/doc checks run; unrun ones stay pending duties.
213	4. **Finalize and synchronize.** Acceptance authorizes that candidate's
214	   pending finalize: direct its owning worker to finalize and merge, then verify
215	   remote, Issue, archive, doc docking, and cleanup results: lifecycle facts,
216	   not QA PASS ([doc-maintenance](references/doc-maintenance.md)).
217	   Prefer one run at a time; judge safe concurrency. After the baseline moves, direct affected owners to save
218	   work and rebase/update at a safe boundary. Review conflicts and revalidate changes; do not switch HEAD
219	   mid-measurement or reuse invalidated evidence. History rewriting needs applicable authorization.
220	   When records are inconsistent, investigate and direct a scoped repair;
221	   never fabricate claim identities.
222	5. **Reclaim seats and report.** The only legal idle seat is one whose delivery is
223	   awaiting acceptance; a rejected delivery's repair is the same assignment unless substantive (task-failure),
224	   and an accepted seat keeps only the finalize/cleanup duties it owns. Once
225	   it owns none (done or explicitly handed off) or the seat is abandoned,
226	   exact-stop it in that same beat. The stop action is the exact owned session
227	   `stop` via the matching platform Skill, which ends its ACP holder. Idle is not
228	   keep-alive or completion. New authorized work or another task gets a fresh
229	   `start` under a new standard name, never a finished seat;
230	   `--resume`/`--continue` recover the same assignment only.
231	
232	   A Host with in-flight/delivery/acceptance/close-out is not an idle worker;
233	   keep it; send it no "continue". Next beat: worker event. Before quiescence
234	   reconcile owner/heartbeat project.goal/stop and QA/docs; worker done ends no
235	   open mandate. [duty-reconcile.md](references/duty-reconcile.md).
236	   Claim only with intake open. Blocked duties keep next action/reopening condition
237	   in existing heartbeat values. Assignment-local retry bounds never pause project;
238	   owner/project bounds keep scope. Worker stop/replacement never resets attempt limits.
239	   Ending a run: stop/pause/cleanup. Session stop is not issue closure;
240	   acceptance/merge/cleanup differ.
241	
242	## Ending a run
243	
244	When ending a project run, finish every in-hand authorized task and each
245	claimed/in-flight issue of this run; merge their worktrees/branches, remove
246	branch tails, and clean the workspace per Kaola Workflow close-out. Do not park
247	unfinished branches as the normal end.
248	
249	Do not accept or dispatch new tasks after the stop boundary. Do not claim or
250	start new issues. After time-up, still finish in-hand and merge/clean.
251	
252	The time/condition boundary is not the scoped pause. Only an explicit owner
253	"stop here and continue later" with stated scope skips cleanup and permits
254	recovery-preserving branches; do not merge or clean beyond that scope.
255	
256	## Report
257	
258	Use the user's report format; otherwise one compact current-work table plus
259	outstanding close-out and pending QA items. Include task/progress, meaningful
260	model mismatches, blockers, and next action. For non-pool seats, per platform report `live N /
261	authorized M` and the seats stopped this beat; N > M with no stop that beat
262	violates the cap. Pool seats report live seats marked exempt. Drop stale stopped rows from reports. Keep duties traceable in
263	existing records and reuse existing Runner `stop`/`start`: no session state
264	machine, quota engine, or close-out dashboard or ledger.

1	---
2	name: kimi-cli-kaola-project-runner
3	description: Use when the controlling Agent should communicate with a Kimi Code CLI main conversation through an exact owned ACP session by starting it, reading evidence, sending Agent-selected prompts or keys, reading replies, and stopping only that session.
4	---
5	
6	# Kimi CLI Kaola Project Runner
7	
8	This Skill is a communication driver for Kimi CLI. It gives the controlling Agent a
9	measured ACP channel to one exact owned session; it does not choose commands, Workflow modes, cadence, state, approvals,
10	retries, or completion policy. The separate Skill `kaola-project-runner` (display name Project
11	Runner) is the main orchestrator when a host Agent is supervising workers; this Skill stays
12	transport-only.
13	
14	## Transport
15	
16	ACP is the only transport (Issue #130). The ACP command is `kimi acp`; prompts travel over its stdio JSON-RPC, never shell eval. Login is a human act outside the Runner and needs no terminal. This platform's ACP quirks are in [references/acp.md](references/acp.md) — open it when a quirk matters. A request for the retired PTY transport is refused with `transport-pty-retired` and changes nothing.
17	
18	| `mutation_status` | Safe interpretation |
19	|---|---|
20	| `not_started` | No prompt write began. |
21	| `accepted` | The agent accepted the prompt. |
22	| `in_progress` | Work may already be mutating state. |
23	| `completed` | The turn reached a reported stop reason. |
24	| `unknown` | Partial mutation cannot be ruled out. |
25	
26	Runner never auto-falls back or resends, and never restarts or resumes a session on its own. Read the receipt and decide whether another prompt is appropriate.
27	
28	## Communication loop
29	
30	Resolve this Skill's installed directory once and call its scripts by absolute path — the install
31	destination may contain spaces, and the user's project is passed only through `--repo` (relative
32	paths in these references resolve against the Skill, never the project cwd). Progressive
33	disclosure: open a reference only when the current operation needs it, run the scripts and never read their source, and prefer bounded
34	receipts (`observe`, `status`, `capture --lines`) over whole-history dumps — `capture --full` is an
35	explicit, unbounded request:
36	
37	```bash
38	SKILL_DIR="/absolute/path/to/kimi-cli-kaola-project-runner"   # the directory containing this file
39	REPO="/abs/canonical/root"   # canonical Git root, not a linked worktree
40	SESSION="<exact-name>"   # under Project Runner: <platform>-<CODE>-i<ISSUE>-<purpose>
41	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" preflight --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
42	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" start --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
43	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" observe --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
44	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" capture --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION" --lines 200
45	```
46	
47	The controlling Agent owns model selection for each `start`. This Skill declares its per-run
48	presets — `--tier default` (**Kimi K3**: `kimi-code/k3`, thinking=max) and `--tier kimi-k2-8` (**Kimi K2.8**: `kimi-code/kimi-for-coding`, thinking=max) — and `default` applies whenever nothing more specific was chosen. Pass
49	another `--tier` when the human or an existing authorization — the default-authorized Worker pool included —
50	names that preset; never infer one from code size, failures, elapsed time, or your own assessment.
51	An undeclared name is refused (`tier-not-declared`), never resolved to `default`.
52	
53	An explicit user model choice always wins: pass it with `--model ID`, adding `--effort LEVEL` only
54	when the user also named an effort. A bare explicit `--model` leaves the runtime's native effort
55	alone — never attach a preset's effort to a different model. If the user picks a model ID that
56	already encodes effort or Fast (such as a `-fast` variant), pass it as-is; the Runner does not
57	invent extra effort or Fast configuration for it.
58	
59	Fast is OFF by default. Pass `--fast on` only on an explicit user request for Fast; this platform's
60	Fast support: no native Fast toggle; speed-named catalog models such as kimi-code/kimi-for-coding-highspeed are explicit model choices, not a Fast switch. Fast and tier are independent selections. When a native fast model
61	ID is what the user explicitly selected, it counts as the explicit Fast selection — report the
62	conflict honestly if it is also passed with `--fast off`.
63	
64	`preflight` and `start` report the requested and resolved selection, and `start` what it applied
65	(`config_application`, `effective_selection`), including unavailable, unsupported, and unknown
66	outcomes; `observe`/`status` show the agent's `configOptions` `currentValue`. `--resume`/`--continue`
67	preserve the saved native session model and effort unless the caller supplies `--tier`, `--model`,
68	or `--effort`; Fast stays a per-run request (off unless explicitly on). All of this is per-run
69	input and never rewrites global CLI configuration. A mismatch or unreadable actual model remains
70	evidence for the Agent and does not disable the communication channel.
71	
72	`preflight` reports runtime and optional Kaola carrier evidence. Missing Workflow commands,
73	configuration health, account state, activity hints, or a changed
74	snapshot do not authorize or block starting the CLI communication channel.
75	
76	Use the evidence internally to choose the next communication action. Do not narrate raw holder,
77	process, snapshot, model, or activity fields in user progress updates; report only visible
78	task progress, an actual transport failure, or a decision that genuinely needs the user.
79	
80	After reading current evidence, the controlling Agent chooses what to send:
81	
82	```bash
83	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" send --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION" --text '<agent-selected prompt>'
84	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" observe --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
85	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" capture --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION" --lines 200
86	```
87	
88	## Steering a running turn
89	
90	Kimi CLI's ACP surface exposes no native mid-turn entry, so a bare `steer`
91	refuses and writes nothing. The available path is the composite, which you
92	choose explicitly:
93	
94	```bash
95	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" steer --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION" \
96	  --steer-mode interrupt --text '<redirection>'
97	```
98	
99	It **cancels** the running turn, confirms it stopped, then sends your text as the
100	next turn on the same session, which keeps the conversation's context. That is
101	interrupted-then-continued, never injection: work in progress stops and may have
102	left partial side effects (`side_effects_possible`). An unconfirmed cancel sends
103	nothing and reports `unknown`. See [references/steering.md](references/steering.md).
104	
105	## Cancel and permissions
106	
107	`key --key escape` (or `cancel`) cancels the running turn; there are no other native keys, menus,
108	or editor replacement. Settle a pending permission `request_id` with
109	`permit [--request-id ID] --option OPTION_ID` (an option the request offers); omitting `--option`
110	answers `cancelled`, which denies. Read the resulting output before choosing another action.
111	
112	Permission default: `start` sets ACP `mode=yolo`; `--permission-mode MODE` sets another advertised `mode` value.
113	
114	When the Agent decides the exact session is finished, end only that owned session:
115	
116	```bash
117	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" stop --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
118	"$SKILL_DIR/scripts/runtime-tmux.sh" status --repo "$REPO" --session "$SESSION"
119	```
120	
121	Use `--force` only when the Agent explicitly chooses forced containment for this exact owned
122	session. Never use broad session/process cleanup, and never reconstruct ownership from process
123	names or fuzzy session matches.
124	
125	## Ending, releasing, and resuming
126	
127	The controlling Agent owns every completion judgment; the Runner executes the chosen operation
128	and reports the true result. These are operation facts, never gates:
129	
130	- A finished reply is not a finished task: an `end_turn` event, an idle terminal, or a
131	  successful `send` receipt never establishes completion.
132	- `stop` releases the owned runtime (the ACP holder and its agent). It never deletes CLI
133	  history, session records, work artifacts, or unrelated resources. Judge success by the
134	  `stop`/`status` result evidence, not by a completed call.
135	- Before stopping, the Agent may keep available resume facts (platform, canonical repo, any
136	  reported native session ID, outcome, remaining work) from existing receipts and Workflow
137	  records. The native session ID is the CLI's own conversation identifier, never the Runner's
138	  `--session` name. Missing identifiers never block a chosen `stop`.
139	- Later work resumes by the Agent's choice: `start --resume <native-session-id>`,
140	  `start --continue` for the platform's latest conversation, or a fresh `start` plus existing
141	  records where the platform cannot resume.
142	
143	## Optional Kaola Workflow
144	
145	Ordinary Workflow-backed work binds `--repo` to the consuming project's canonical Git root and asks this CLI to invoke its installed
146	`workflow-next`, so that runtime's Workflow creates or recovers the child worktree; this Skill only
147	transports the exact session. Linked-worktree starts, outer-prepared bundles, and existing-run
148	recovery are Agent decisions, not transport gates. A session already in a child worktree is advisory: preserve work, then continue,
149	stop/restart at root, or use another Workflow recovery path. Installation for another runtime alone
150	does not establish availability here.
151	
152	## Evidence boundary
153	
154	- `capture`, events, process facts, permission facts, activity hints, and snapshot changes are
155	  evidence for the Agent.
156	- Exact session ownership, platform/repository identity, holder identity, prompt fingerprinting,
157	  and outbound redaction are transport integrity checks.
158	- The Runner never classifies evidence into permission to act. The Agent handles every runtime or
159	  Workflow problem after reading the evidence.
160	- No invocation implicitly starts `workflow-next`, installs commands, materializes repository files,
161	  creates a heartbeat, or selects recurring behavior. The Agent may send any of those commands when
162	  it decides they serve the user's task.
163	
164	See [references/platform.md](references/platform.md) for Kimi CLI launch/observation facts
165	and [references/acp.md](references/acp.md) for the structured ACP command surface.

2	name: kaola-project-runner
3	description: "Use when the controlling Agent should supervise explicitly authorized CLI workers through the ten platform Runner Skills: recover live authorization, dispatch and review work, accept deliveries before finalize, cap live workers at the authorized count, and stop each accepted seat without dropping close-out duties."
4	---
5	
6	# Project Runner
7	
8	This Skill is the main control-plane Skill. It is not a platform Runner and has
9	no transport adapter. The ten platform Runner Skills are workers: they only
10	identify, start, send, wait, permit, observe, capture, and stop an exact owned
11	session. Kaola-Workflow, when used, owns worker-side claim, mission ledger,
12	child worktree, finalize, archive, and sink.
13	
14	One Host owns the plan, acceptance and QA.
15	Helpers do bounded planning, research, QA, synthesis, explicitly scoped light work
16	or an assignment. They never scale, control workers, run another scheduling loop,
17	grant permission or accept the project.
18	You pick presets, write assignments, dispatch, judge originals;
19	Sideagent nodes reconcile batches: [lifecycle-state.md](references/lifecycle-state.md), [node](references/sideagent-node.md).
20	Read, search, analyze and do simple authorized work. Larger code, test or doc work goes to workers
21	unless the human allows self-execution.
22	
23	Authorized release/install mechanics may stay Host-owned without an issue or
24	worker just for them; honor owner allocation and project lifecycle.
25	
26	## Two entry points
27	
28	**Standalone/non-Host supervision** - use the loop below without Host event binding.
29	
30	**Host** - you are already a named Host session that loaded this Skill through
31	the native `/kaola-project-runner` Skill invocation (ZCode) or your platform's
32	measured entry, and supervise workers on event-driven beats. Outer Agents
33	start or continue the Host through Kaola-Delegator (`kaola-delegator`).
34	Use existing project plans for role, authorization and lifecycle; this Skill
35	creates none. Startup and one Host per root (`host-exists`), plus a
36	Delegator-inquiry sweep (one owned permission event needs no full sweep):
37	[host-startup.md](references/host-startup.md) ·
38	[zcode-native-skill-entry.md](references/zcode-native-skill-entry.md) ·
39	[host-entry-matrix.md](references/host-entry-matrix.md).
40	A Host (any platform with a `host_skill_entry`) is event-driven: no
41	Routine, cron, or sleep loop. Its first prompt names its
42	`platform`/`session`/`repo`; `KAOLA_ACP_DISPATCHER` carries them to its shell.
43	Every Host assignment uses `--no-wait`, then ends the turn, including direct
44	Runner/Workflow, continuation, repair and finalize. Beat mechanics - ending the turn as the wait: [references/zcode-host-dispatch.md](references/zcode-host-dispatch.md).
45	Each inner worker is its own session and process group: an inner stop never
46	reaches the Host; the Host's stop sweeps only recorded inner sessions.
47	Grok Bot is not an entry for this Skill: it loads generated `kaola-delegator`,
48	which starts one Host of any platform that loads this Skill. `--platform grok` is the
49	Grok CLI worker; `--platform grok-bot` is invalid. Do not create a Grok Bot
50	Routine to run this Skill. Keep the Host shell cwd at the canonical root: never
51	`cd` into a worktree finalize/sink may remove; use absolute paths, `git -C`, or
52	`(cd ... && ...)`.
53	
54	## Consumer-project boundary
55	
56	For consumer-project work, the Project Runner checkout, templates, generated
57	files, and installed Skill payload are read-only. Store project-specific
58	authorization, heartbeat, and run facts in the consuming project. Do not edit
59	any of the above unless a human explicitly assigned Project Runner
60	development.
61	
62	## Authorization
63	
64	Recover existing explicit authorization and live work before asking intake
65	questions. A Skill update or resumed conversation must not restart intake,
66	workers, claims or assignments already established. Ask only for missing or
67	conflicting information.
68	
69	Record the human's CLI, model/effort, count, and capability restrictions in the
70	consuming project's run records, not in this Skill. The count is a hard cap on
71	live worker processes, ACP holders included; a finished seat counts until its
72	`stop` receipt. Granted open-ended concurrency is its own cap. Do not invent a
73	quota system: the cap is that count, enforced from `status`/`stop` receipts.
74	Preset classes ([worker-profiles.md](references/worker-profiles.md)): five
75	Worker presets are default-authorized outside that cap (permission, not
76	preference); Elite needs an explicit grant; Expert is complex thinking only,
77	under an explicit standing grant or fresh user permission per task. Delegate substantial planning, design or
78	review to an available authorized seat when its profile or the owner's
79	task-specific judgment makes it a better fit than your own known model/preset.
80	The heartbeat holds the three Class meanings and a compact capability
81	summary. Catalog profiles stay in
82	[profile-catalog.md](references/profile-catalog.md). Exact grants stay in the
83	heartbeat authorization. At a dispatch decision, project eligible candidates
84	instead of keeping the profile roster in routine context
85	([dispatch-collect.md](references/dispatch-collect.md)).
86	
87	Obey owner/project and single-writer rules. Holds stop only source-named actions.
88	Distinguish implementation prerequisites, merge order and resource occupancy;
89	a copied Host summary alone establishes no dependency. Unaffected authorized
90	work proceeds.
91	
92	### Selected platform
93	
94	Call the matching platform Runner by its installed directory
95	`<id>-kaola-project-runner`. Every platform's default transport is ACP.
96	
97	### Progressive disclosure
98	
99	This Skill loads on its own. Load one selected worker Skill only at dispatch, a
100	reference only when the current step needs it, and never read script source or
101	whole files into context: receipts, hashes, counts and bounded excerpts are the
102	evidence. Ordinary `observe`, `status` and `capture --lines` receipts stay bounded
103	(`truncated` names dropped fields); `capture --full` is the only unbounded
104	request.
105	Never log in, relogin, switch accounts, or repair credentials. A confirmed limit or account refusal follows [quota-packages.md](references/quota-packages.md); that rule does not change the count cap.
106	
107	### Defaults
108	
109	| Item | Default / rule |
110	|---|---|
111	| Allowed CLIs | See Authorization above. No authorized task: ask; start no worker or heartbeat. |
112	| Count | Named CLI without a count: one; it bounds live processes. |
113	| Model / transport | Platform `--tier default`, Fast off, default transport. Explicit human choices win. Resume preserves saved native choices. |
114	| Other tiers | Only default is common; tiers are platform-specific/unranked. No automatic model, tier, or transport switch; only owner-authorized model/preset changes stay within runtime. |
115	| Workflow | On. If explicitly off or unavailable, use authorized PR/verification delivery and disclose the limitation; do not fake Workflow records. |
116	| Heartbeat | Non-Host: 30 minutes unless specified; zero or "no heartbeat" means one-shot; one host-native carrier, else same-session sleep, never both. Host beats are event-driven (Heartbeat). |
117	| Permissions | Per platform, not one global bypass. Honor explicit permission-mode overrides. Ordinary approval leftovers are handled here within authorized scope, not routinely sent to the human. |
118	| Cursor | Never use `/model` as a read-only probe. |
119	
120	Bind the consuming project's canonical project root once at setup with
121	`export KAOLA_PROJECT_RUNNER_CANONICAL_REPO=<abs root>`, then omit `--repo`; the
122	Runner fills it and refuses a drifted root at start. Ask each worker to invoke its installed
123	workflow-next. Without that binding, linked-worktree starts and existing-run
124	recovery are Agent decisions, not transport gates. See
125	[workflow-worktree.md](references/workflow-worktree.md).
126	
127	Model mismatches are evidence, not automatic start gates. Bypass is not broader authorization. With no verified ACP skip-all,
128	permission may still arise: `permit` settles it; never add a gate.
129	
130	## Heartbeat
131	
132	The heartbeat is the working prompt itself: a Host (any platform with a
133	`host_skill_entry`) runs it on each worker event; Codex's own timer serves only
134	a non-Host Codex supervisor; host-native carriers. Its `body` is one JSON object per
135	[heartbeat-skeleton.md](references/heartbeat-skeleton.md), written
136	only by `state`. It is the effective-now snapshot, not a
137	log: update changed facts/duties, replacing superseded quota, priority and
138	plans, keeping in-flight locators and unfinished duties. A confirmed change
139	applies in that beat; decision-boundary adoption:
140	[duty-reconcile.md](references/duty-reconcile.md); a lowered quota alone cancels nothing. A report-only
141	request disables execution actions. When an updated Skill loads, reconcile the
142	heartbeat once with current rules, latest valid instructions and fresh seat
143	facts, keeping user limits and the frontier (v1: `state migrate`).
144	
145	After close-out, cancel the native heartbeat or stop scheduling the next
146	sleep. Having no ready task now is not
147	project completion. Do not hard-code other hosts' scheduler APIs.
148	
149	## Delivery
150	
151	Prefer the selected, authorized Workflow sync/merge when a PR is not required:
152	a PR is not opened merely for handoff when that sink is suitable.
153	If PRs exist, advance actionable ones first on contested suitable
154	capacity; other authorized work continues in parallel across permitted CLIs.
155	A blocked PR keeps an owner and next action without a global hold. Honor
156	acceptance, explicit PR requests, branch protection, stop-intake, selected
157	sink, and write ownership.
158	
159	## Main execution loop
160	
161	1. **Recover and observe.** Load compact current state as needed on a new
162	   turn or recovery; reuse facts already read this turn. Read only fresh
163	   worker/run, Git/Forge and Runner facts relevant to the next decision. Use exact owned sessions and
164	   current platform Skills. Observe busy workers without injecting "status?"
165	   messages or polling raw frames as a human UI. Do not replay a prompt whose
166	   acceptance or effects are known or uncertain; investigate the existing action
167	   first. Steering a running turn is an Agent
168	   choice, never a Runner policy: pick the mode yourself, read the receipt, and
169	   never call a not-consumed or `unknown` steer delivered.
170	2. **Decide and dispatch.** Resolve worker questions within existing
171	   authorization; escalate only major structural, value, or extra-authority
172	   decisions. `HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED` is considered by the orchestrator
173	   first. A seat whose `status` says `stale: true` is not a dispatch target;
174	   an operator-confirmed exception on that one `send`/`steer` is the
175	   orchestrator's own call; replace it with `drain-restart` at idle
176	   (zcode-host-dispatch.md).
177	   Examine authorized remaining work. Give each clear task directly to a suitable authorized worker as a new session, chosen from the current eligible-candidate projection by owner direction, class responsibility, profile/task fit and capacity; past dispatch or success informs that choice, never replaces it. Split or parallelize when independent parts gain real time or coverage. The count is a ceiling, not a target to fill; never invent work or expand authorization. At the hard cap, stop one seat before starting any new one (stop-before-start).
178	   Before planning, assigning or judging QA, read
179	   [qa-evidence.md](references/qa-evidence.md) unless the current version is
180	   already in context. Planned dispatch (research, QA, report or
181	   implementation) uses `execute`
182	   ([dispatch-collect.md](references/dispatch-collect.md)): it starts absent
183	   seats at the preset `--tier` and records their facts. Direct Runner
184	   `start`/`send` is standalone, degraded or same-assignment recovery
185	   (zcode-host-dispatch.md). No permission-mode override unless the human
186	   wrote one. One dispatch prompt per ready session. External knowledge gap behind a route, obstacle, failure or QA question: [public-research.md](references/public-research.md). You still accept and exact-stop. State the task,
187	   working location, write ownership, constraints, delivery requirements, and
188	   the doc-impact call in its prompt, plus whether Workflow is on. That prompt
189	   carries the assignment only: never orchestration policy or the seat roster.
190	   The worker must not self-finalize before acceptance; irreversible or value
191	   choices print `HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED` and wait. Merely seeing a
192	   worktree or ledger is not write authorization. Same-file collaboration needs explicit
193	   coordination and an integrator, not a blanket disjointness rule. Do not
194	   expand the authorized goal or duplicate claims. Pass still-valid candidate
195	   evidence; recheck changed/invalidated facts or actual gaps. Keep required
196	   project/release checks. Substantive failure: [task-failure.md](references/task-failure.md).
197	   One run claims one real issue: never a bundle claim, worktree, ledger or
198	   session spanning several, and collaborating workers share that issue's run under
199	   distinct names. Choose the real open issue before start, name the session
200	   `<platform>-<CODE>-i<ISSUE>-<purpose>` (`droid-KT-i274-parser`) with `CODE` the
201	   heartbeat's declared project short code, verify it in the start receipt, and
202	   keep the rule on later dispatches and restarts. Hosts, diagnostics and
203	   issue-less tasks carry no issue number and never an invented one. Detail:
204	   [issue-dispatch.md](references/issue-dispatch.md).
205	3. **Accept the delivery.** Mission-frontier done triggers review, not automatic finalize. When a worker
206	   claims completion, judge its actual diff, checks, docs and run records
207	   against that assignment under the effective global Workflow rules. Reuse
208	   sufficient evidence for this candidate; return only concrete routine deviations,
209	   omissions or invalidated evidence to that worker, and never finalize on
210	   incomplete evidence or lowered assertions. Worker prose, idle, green CI or
211	   a successful script exit is not acceptance, and acceptance is not project
212	   QA: you pick when aggregate QA/doc checks run; unrun ones stay pending duties.
213	4. **Finalize and synchronize.** Acceptance authorizes that candidate's
214	   pending finalize: direct its owning worker to finalize and merge, then verify
215	   remote, Issue, archive, doc docking, and cleanup results: lifecycle facts,
216	   not QA PASS ([doc-maintenance](references/doc-maintenance.md)).
217	   Prefer one run at a time; judge safe concurrency. After the baseline moves, direct affected owners to save
218	   work and rebase/update at a safe boundary. Review conflicts and revalidate changes; do not switch HEAD
219	   mid-measurement or reuse invalidated evidence. History rewriting needs applicable authorization.
220	   When records are inconsistent, investigate and direct a scoped repair;
221	   never fabricate claim identities.
222	5. **Reclaim seats and report.** The only legal idle seat is one whose delivery is
223	   awaiting acceptance; a rejected delivery's repair is the same assignment unless substantive (task-failure),
224	   and an accepted seat keeps only the finalize/cleanup duties it owns. Once
225	   it owns none (done or explicitly handed off) or the seat is abandoned,
226	   exact-stop it in that same beat. The stop action is the exact owned session
227	   `stop` via the matching platform Skill, which ends its ACP holder. Idle is not
228	   keep-alive or completion. New authorized work or another task gets a fresh
229	   `start` under a new standard name, never a finished seat;
230	   `--resume`/`--continue` recover the same assignment only.
231	
232	   A Host with in-flight/delivery/acceptance/close-out is not an idle worker;
233	   keep it; send it no "continue". Next beat: worker event. Before quiescence
234	   reconcile owner/heartbeat project.goal/stop and QA/docs; worker done ends no
235	   open mandate. [duty-reconcile.md](references/duty-reconcile.md).
236	   Claim only with intake open. Blocked duties keep next action/reopening condition
237	   in existing heartbeat values. Assignment-local retry bounds never pause project;
238	   owner/project bounds keep scope. Worker stop/replacement never resets attempt limits.
239	   Ending a run: stop/pause/cleanup. Session stop is not issue closure;
240	   acceptance/merge/cleanup differ.
241	
242	## Ending a run
243	
244	When ending a project run, finish every in-hand authorized task and each
245	claimed/in-flight issue of this run; merge their worktrees/branches, remove
246	branch tails, and clean the workspace per Kaola Workflow close-out. Do not park
247	unfinished branches as the normal end.
248	
249	Do not accept or dispatch new tasks after the stop boundary. Do not claim or
250	start new issues. After time-up, still finish in-hand and merge/clean.
251	
252	The time/condition boundary is not the scoped pause. Only an explicit owner
253	"stop here and continue later" with stated scope skips cleanup and permits
254	recovery-preserving branches; do not merge or clean beyond that scope.
255	
256	## Report
257	
258	Use the user's report format; otherwise one compact current-work table plus
259	outstanding close-out and pending QA items. Include task/progress, meaningful
260	model mismatches, blockers, and next action. For non-pool seats, per platform report `live N /
261	authorized M` and the seats stopped this beat; N > M with no stop that beat
262	violates the cap. Pool seats report live seats marked exempt. Drop stale stopped rows from reports. Keep duties traceable in
263	existing records and reuse existing Runner `stop`/`start`: no session state
264	machine, quota engine, or close-out dashboard or ledger.

127	Model mismatches are evidence, not automatic start gates. Bypass is not broader authorization. With no verified ACP skip-all,
128	permission may still arise: `permit` settles it; never add a gate.
129	
130	## Heartbeat
131	
132	The heartbeat is the working prompt itself: a Host (any platform with a
133	`host_skill_entry`) runs it on each worker event; Codex's own timer serves only
134	a non-Host Codex supervisor; host-native carriers. Its `body` is one JSON object per
135	[heartbeat-skeleton.md](references/heartbeat-skeleton.md), written
136	only by `state`. It is the effective-now snapshot, not a
137	log: update changed facts/duties, replacing superseded quota, priority and
138	plans, keeping in-flight locators and unfinished duties. A confirmed change
139	applies in that beat; decision-boundary adoption:
140	[duty-reconcile.md](references/duty-reconcile.md); a lowered quota alone cancels nothing. A report-only
141	request disables execution actions. When an updated Skill loads, reconcile the
142	heartbeat once with current rules, latest valid instructions and fresh seat
143	facts, keeping user limits and the frontier (v1: `state migrate`).
144	
145	After close-out, cancel the native heartbeat or stop scheduling the next
146	sleep. Having no ready task now is not
147	project completion. Do not hard-code other hosts' scheduler APIs.
148	
149	## Delivery
150	
151	Prefer the selected, authorized Workflow sync/merge when a PR is not required:
152	a PR is not opened merely for handoff when that sink is suitable.
153	If PRs exist, advance actionable ones first on contested suitable
154	capacity; other authorized work continues in parallel across permitted CLIs.
155	A blocked PR keeps an owner and next action without a global hold. Honor
156	acceptance, explicit PR requests, branch protection, stop-intake, selected
157	sink, and write ownership.
158	
159	## Main execution loop
160	
161	1. **Recover and observe.** Load compact current state as needed on a new
162	   turn or recovery; reuse facts already read this turn. Read only fresh
163	   worker/run, Git/Forge and Runner facts relevant to the next decision. Use exact owned sessions and
164	   current platform Skills. Observe busy workers without injecting "status?"
165	   messages or polling raw frames as a human UI. Do not replay a prompt whose
166	   acceptance or effects are known or uncertain; investigate the existing action
167	   first. Steering a running turn is an Agent
168	   choice, never a Runner policy: pick the mode yourself, read the receipt, and
169	   never call a not-consumed or `unknown` steer delivered.
170	2. **Decide and dispatch.** Resolve worker questions within existing
171	   authorization; escalate only major structural, value, or extra-authority
172	   decisions. `HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED` is considered by the orchestrator
173	   first. A seat whose `status` says `stale: true` is not a dispatch target;
174	   an operator-confirmed exception on that one `send`/`steer` is the
175	   orchestrator's own call; replace it with `drain-restart` at idle
176	   (zcode-host-dispatch.md).
177	   Examine authorized remaining work. Give each clear task directly to a suitable authorized worker as a new session, chosen from the current eligible-candidate projection by owner direction, class responsibility, profile/task fit and capacity; past dispatch or success informs that choice, never replaces it. Split or parallelize when independent parts gain real time or coverage. The count is a ceiling, not a target to fill; never invent work or expand authorization. At the hard cap, stop one seat before starting any new one (stop-before-start).
178	   Before planning, assigning or judging QA, read
179	   [qa-evidence.md](references/qa-evidence.md) unless the current version is
180	   already in context. Planned dispatch (research, QA, report or
181	   implementation) uses `execute`
182	   ([dispatch-collect.md](references/dispatch-collect.md)): it starts absent
183	   seats at the preset `--tier` and records their facts. Direct Runner
184	   `start`/`send` is standalone, degraded or same-assignment recovery
185	   (zcode-host-dispatch.md). No permission-mode override unless the human
186	   wrote one. One dispatch prompt per ready session. External knowledge gap behind a route, obstacle, failure or QA question: [public-research.md](references/public-research.md). You still accept and exact-stop. State the task,
187	   working location, write ownership, constraints, delivery requirements, and
188	   the doc-impact call in its prompt, plus whether Workflow is on. That prompt
189	   carries the assignment only: never orchestration policy or the seat roster.
190	   The worker must not self-finalize before acceptance; irreversible or value
191	   choices print `HUMAN_DECISION_REQUIRED` and wait. Merely seeing a
192	   worktree or ledger is not write authorization. Same-file collaboration needs explicit
193	   coordination and an integrator, not a blanket disjointness rule. Do not
194	   expand the authorized goal or duplicate claims. Pass still-valid candidate
195	   evidence; recheck changed/invalidated facts or actual gaps. Keep required
196	   project/release checks. Substantive failure: [task-failure.md](references/task-failure.md).
197	   One run claims one real issue: never a bundle claim, worktree, ledger or
198	   session spanning several, and collaborating workers share that issue's run under
199	   distinct names. Choose the real open issue before start, name the session
200	   `<platform>-<CODE>-i<ISSUE>-<purpose>` (`droid-KT-i274-parser`) with `CODE` the
201	   heartbeat's declared project short code, verify it in the start receipt, and
202	   keep the rule on later dispatches and restarts. Hosts, diagnostics and
203	   issue-less tasks carry no issue number and never an invented one. Detail:
204	   [issue-dispatch.md](references/issue-dispatch.md).
205	3. **Accept the delivery.** Mission-frontier done triggers review, not automatic finalize. When a worker
206	   claims completion, judge its actual diff, checks, docs and run records
207	   against that assignment under the effective global Workflow rules. Reuse
208	   sufficient evidence for this candidate; return only concrete routine deviations,
209	   omissions or invalidated evidence to that worker, and never finalize on
210	   incomplete evidence or lowered assertions. Worker prose, idle, green CI or
211	   a successful script exit is not acceptance, and acceptance is not project
212	   QA: you pick when aggregate QA/doc checks run; unrun ones stay pending duties.
213	4. **Finalize and synchronize.** Acceptance authorizes that candidate's
214	   pending finalize: direct its owning worker to finalize and merge, then verify
215	   remote, Issue, archive, doc docking, and cleanup results: lifecycle facts,
216	   not QA PASS ([doc-maintenance](references/doc-maintenance.md)).
217	   Prefer one run at a time; judge safe concurrency. After the baseline moves, direct affected owners to save
218	   work and rebase/update at a safe boundary. Review conflicts and revalidate changes; do not switch HEAD
219	   mid-measurement or reuse invalidated evidence. History rewriting needs applicable authorization.
220	   When records are inconsistent, investigate and direct a scoped repair;
221	   never fabricate claim identities.
222	5. **Reclaim seats and report.** The only legal idle seat is one whose delivery is
223	   awaiting acceptance; a rejected delivery's repair is the same assignment unless substantive (task-failure),
224	   and an accepted seat keeps only the finalize/cleanup duties it owns. Once
225	   it owns none (done or explicitly handed off) or the seat is abandoned,
226	   exact-stop it in that same beat. The stop action is the exact owned session
227	   `stop` via the matching platform Skill, which ends its ACP holder. Idle is not
228	   keep-alive or completion. New authorized work or another task gets a fresh
229	   `start` under a new standard name, never a finished seat;
230	   `--resume`/`--continue` recover the same assignment only.
231	
232	   A Host with in-flight/delivery/acceptance/close-out is not an idle worker;
233	   keep it; send it no "continue". Next beat: worker event. Before quiescence
234	   reconcile owner/heartbeat project.goal/stop and QA/docs; worker done ends no
235	   open mandate. [duty-reconcile.md](references/duty-reconcile.md).
236	   Claim only with intake open. Blocked duties keep next action/reopening condition
237	   in existing heartbeat values. Assignment-local retry bounds never pause project;
238	   owner/project bounds keep scope. Worker stop/replacement never resets attempt limits.
239	   Ending a run: stop/pause/cleanup. Session stop is not issue closure;
240	   acceptance/merge/cleanup differ.
241	
242	## Ending a run
243	
244	When ending a project run, finish every in-hand authorized task and each
245	claimed/in-flight issue of this run; merge their worktrees/branches, remove
246	branch tails, and clean the workspace per Kaola Workflow close-out. Do not park
247	unfinished branches as the normal end.
248	
249	Do not accept or dispatch new tasks after the stop boundary. Do not claim or
250	start new issues. After time-up, still finish in-hand and merge/clean.
251	
252	The time/condition boundary is not the scoped pause. Only an explicit owner
253	"stop here and continue later" with stated scope skips cleanup and permits
254	recovery-preserving branches; do not merge or clean beyond that scope.
255	
256	## Report
257	
258	Use the user's report format; otherwise one compact current-work table plus
259	outstanding close-out and pending QA items. Include task/progress, meaningful
260	model mismatches, blockers, and next action. For non-pool seats, per platform report `live N /
261	authorized M` and the seats stopped this beat; N > M with no stop that beat
262	violates the cap. Pool seats report live seats marked exempt. Drop stale stopped rows from reports. Keep duties traceable in
263	existing records and reuse existing Runner `stop`/`start`: no session state
264	machine, quota engine, or close-out dashboard or ledger.
